newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firm, April Dubai trades kicks off.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firm, April Dubai trades kicks off.

text.p: Asian crude prices were slightly firmer on Thursday in generally quiet trade with deals for next-month trading already taking place.
Traders said two Dubai wet cargoes for April may have already traded on the basis of March quotes +19 cents, roughly in line with value based on a spread of 38 cents.
Otherwise the MidEast market had wound down, traders said.
They estimated that March Oman was now all placed, with a major putting one million barrels into an affiliate in Thailand. Oman went out valued at MPM +10 cents.
Paper spreads were slightly weaker as bidders stood back.
Offers into the India March crude buying tender are due in by later on Thursday and the award should be made late on Friday.
In regional trading, 150,000 barrels of March Belida were heard trading at ICP +80/90 cents, although some players put the price lower at +70 cents.
A Japanese shosha was said to be the seller of the barrels and a U.S. major the buyer.
Most regional grades are not yet talked for March. Nominations are not due into Pertamina until February 10, for allocations a few days later.
A producer was continuing to offer Cossack, Kutubu and Griffin at APPI Tapis quotes plus 20 cents for second half March.
Australian availabilities are tight for March, but supply should be alleviated by the arrival of several 650,000-barrel cargos of West African crude, traders said.
The West African barrels were partly to fill in for shipping delays on Cossack and Griffin after recent cyclones shut down the floating production.
